sources.summary: Company asserts about half of warm-air calls are simple fixes. No sample, denominator, collection window, or reproducible method is disclosed; this verifies an attributed assertion only.
Page reports 40-50% from unidentified industry data, without a linked dataset or denominator. It does not establish that these are the company's own measured outcomes.
Opening text attributes about 50% to three simple causes. Later text assigns roughly half to the first cause alone. No dataset or method resolves that internal inconsistency.
Company describes about half as causes a homeowner can check, without a denominator or outcome dataset. Checkable causes are not identical to confirmed homeowner resolutions.

FAQ publishes $200-$1,500 and describes thermostat fixes as cheaper than compressor/leak work. Troubleshooting covers thermostat, filter and outdoor power. Another FAQ says to stop a warm-blowing system immediately.

Supports immediate cooling shutdown, fan ON while thawing, and possible severe compressor damage. Describes airflow restrictions and refrigerant issues; restart advice requires thawing, restored airflow and dryness.
Supports COOL-to-OFF, major-damage risk and professional repair. This page does not instruct fan ON. Low refrigerant may reflect leakage or improper initial charging.
Published installed range is $100-$400, with hourly labor $75-$150. It supports humming/start symptoms and professional-only replacement. Labor rates alone do not establish a $150 minimum total.
Supports reduced cooling, ice, hissing, nonconsumed refrigerant and professional repair. FAQ publishes $250-$1,600 credited to Angi. It does not specify a weeks-long onset or a $1,600+ range.

Separates condenser cleaning $75-$200 from acid washing $300-$350; maintenance-bundled cleaning is $75-$100. The frozen span combines categories. The guide describes customer surveys plus outside research without a page-specific sample.
Lists common central-AC repairs $150-$650 and evaporator replacement $700-$2,500+. There is no literal frozen-coil $150-$2,500 row. Figures derive from Angi and Home Depot; this is a compilation.

claims.reason: Four websites contain approximate-half assertions; the combined wording overstates their common provenance and resolution measurement. One source repeats unidentified industry data, two describe checkable causes, and no denominator is available.

No independent evidence the asserted frequencies are accurate
